institutions.history: Founded in 1926 as the Alberta College of Art (ACA), the college was originally part of what is now the Southern Alberta Institute of Technology (SAIT). Although the two campuses still border each other, ACA officially separated from SAIT in 1985 to become a stand-alone, independent, publicly funded college of art and design. In 1995 amended its name to become the Alberta College of Art and Design. In 2018, the government of Alberta announced that the college had achieved university status based on the quality of its programs. In 2019, the college received its new name and visual identity as the University of Alberta Arts (AUarts)

institutions.name: Burman University
institutions.history: Founded in 1921 as the Calgary Bible Institute. Became an accredited university college in 1995 and changed its name in 1999 to Nazarene University College (NUC). In 2003, Canadian Bible College (CBC) and Canadian Theological Seminary (CTS) moved to join NUC on the same campus in 2003, received accreditation in 2004, and changed their name to Alliance University College (AUC). AUC and NUC maintained a close relationship, began offering joint programs in 2006, and were often referred to as Alliance University College-Nazarene University College (AUC-NUC), although the two institutions awarded degrees independently until 2007.In 2007, AUC and NUC formed a single entity called Ambrose University. In 2014, province of Alberta granted 'university' nomenclature to Ambrose - Ambrose University College is renamed Ambrose University

institutions.history: Founded in 1921 as Concordia College by the Missouri Synod Lutheran Church. In 1967, Concordia College began offering first-year university courses in affiliation with the University of Alberta. It became a degree-granting university in 1987. In 1995, Concordia College changed its name to Concordia University College of Alberta to reflect its status as a degree granting institution. In 2015, Concordia University College became Concordia University of Edmonton
